newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish army meeting puts pressure on Erbakan.
newsitem.headline: Turkish army meeting puts pressure on Erbakan.

text.p: Turkey's powerful army has brought forward a key meeting in an apparent attempt to put pressure on Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to clamp down on Islamist activism, the media said on Wednesday.

The meeting of the High Military Council, a biannual affair during which promotions, retirements and disciplinary issues are discussed, has been brought forward to May 26 from late summer, according to Turkey's mainstream papers and NTV television.

"Council warning to the Hoja," said Radikal daily, referring to Erbakan by his popular title, meaning "Teacher". Erbakan and Defence Minister Turhan Tayan are due to attend, along with 15 top generals.

Radikal said the military aimed to make Erbakan, who has been stalling on army-led demands to curb Islamist zeal, sign orders for the dismissal of army members deemed to have been involved in Islamist activity.
"The Chief of Staff is planning to give the government an extremely strong message by calling the extraordinary council meeting," Sabah daily said in a front-page article.
The meeting will take place five days before the monthly gathering of the military-dominated National Security Council, which has been putting pressure on Erbakan to commit himself to secularism.
The Islamist-conservative coalition government is also under threat from dissident MPs and the opposition, who are trying to form an Islamist-free alternative alliance.
The government has been deeply divided over the reluctance of Erbakan's Welfare Party to support reforms of the education system which it fears would erode the role of religious schools in Turkey.
